lines: פלת
*פֶּלֶת obsol. root, Arab. فلت to
flee, to escape, i. q. Heb. פָּלַט; فُلْتٌ
swift, فَلَتَانٌ a swift horse, runner.—
Hence the two following.
פֶּלֶת (swiftness) Peleth, pr. n. m. a)
פְּלֵתִי m. (r. פֶּלֶת) a public runner, cou-
rier, with art. collect. the public runners,
couriers, everywhere coupled with כְּרֵתִי
11, 4. 19.  Some without good reason
hold both כְּרֵתִי and פְּלֵתִי to be Philis-
tines, and regard the latter form as put
by paronomasia for פְּלִשְׁתִּי, but against
the analogy of the Hebrew language;
so Ewald Heb. Gram. p. 297.  See in
כְּרֵתִי.
I. פֵּן m. i. q. fem. פִּנָּה which is more
usual, a corner, c. suff. פִּנַּת Prov. 7, 8.
Plur. פִּנִּים Zech. 14, 10.  R. פָּנַן.
II. פֶּן conj. (for פְּנֵה, r. פָּנָה Pi. no. 1)
pr. a removing, taking away; used only
in the constr. state with Makk. פֶּן־, as a
Conj. of removing, prohibiting, hinder-
ing, i. q. μή, that not, lest. Thus:
1. Where an action precedes, that
serves to hinder or prohibit something
which one fears and wishes to remove
or avoid. Gen. 11, 4 let us build us a
city . . . פֶּן־נָפוּץ lest we be scattered. 19,
15 arise . . . פֶּן־תִּסָּפֶה lest thou perish. 3,
3 eat not of it . . . פֶּן־תְּמֻתוּן lest ye die.—
Then, after verbs of fearing, like Gr.
δείδω μή, Lat. vereor ne, Gen. 31, 31,
comp. 26, 9 ; of caution, comp. Gr. ἰδεῖν
μή, Gen. 24, 6. 31, 24. Deut. 4, 23 ; also
of swearing Judg. 15, 12, comp. ὀμνύω μή
Il. 23. 585. In examples of this kind אַל
is never used.
2. At the beginning of a sentence,
where it implies : a) Prohibition or dis-
suasion, like אַל. Job 32, 13 פֶּן־תֹּאמְרוּ
say not, i. e. beware lest ye say. Is. 36,
18 פֶּן־יַסִּית אֶתְכֶם חִזְקִיָּהוּ beware lest
Hezekiah deceive you. b) Fear, appre-
hension, as Gen. 3, 22 וְעַתָּה פֶּן־יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ
וגו׳ and now (I fear) lest he put forth
his hand, etc. 44, 34 פֶּן־אֶרְאֶה בָרָע וגו׳
(I fear) lest I see the evil, etc. 31, 31. 38,
1 Sam. 13, 19. With præt. where one
fears lest something has already taken
פנה
place, 2 Sam. 20, 6 פֶּן־מָצָא lest he may
have found. 2 K. 2, 16 פֶּן־נְשָׂאוֹ רוּחַ יְהוָֹה
(we fear) lest a wind from Jehovah hath
taken him up.—Once it approaches to
the power of a negative adverb, i. q. לֹא,
Prov. 5, 6 אֹרַח חַיִּים פֶּן־תְּפַלֵּס the way of
life she prepareth not for herself, sc. the
adulteress, i. e. she walks not in the way
of life. But the full sentence is: ‘(see)
lest she walk in the way of life.’
פַּנַּג ἅπ. λεγόμ. Ez. 27, 17. perh. a
kind of pastry or sweet cake. The Targ.
renders it קוֹלְיָא, i. e. Gr. κολία, a kind
of sweet pastry; and in the book Zohar
לחם פנג is pastry-work. Other opinions
are enumerated by Celsius in Hierobot.
II. p. 73. Sept. κασία, Vulg. balsamum.
—The etymology is wholly uncertain.
* פָּנָה fut. יִפְנֶה, apoc. and conv.
וַיִּפֶן, יִפֶן, in the other persons וָאֵפֶן,
וַנֵּפֶן, תֵּפֶן; imper. פְּנֵה; to turn, trans. in
one phrase: פָּנָה עֹרֶף to turn the back
where always intrans. to turn, to turn
oneself, i. e.
1. In order to go anywhere, to go
away; Ex. 7, 23 וַיִּפֶן פַּרְעֹה וַיָּבֹא. 10, 6.
16, 7. al. Sometimes with a dat. pleon.
a) to turn to or towards any place, to
betake oneself in any direction, c. עַל
בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִפְנֶה whithersoever he turned
himself; with He parag. 1 K. 17, 3. Deut.
2, 3. Cant. 6, 1. Also with אֶל of pers. to
turn unto any one, to go to him for re-
sponse or for aid, espec. God Is. 45, 22;
angels Job 5, 1; idols Lev. 19, 4. Deut.
31, 18. 20; wicked men Ps. 40, 5; di-
viners Lev. 20, 6; with אֶל of thing, to
turn unto e. g. iniquity Job 36, 21.
פָּנָה אַחֲרֵי פ׳ to turn after any one, to in-
cline to his side or party, Ez. 29, 16.
b) to turn away from any one, c. מֵעִם
Deut. 29, 17 mentally; absol. 30, 17 if
thy heart turn away from God, and thou
do not obey, etc. c) Trop. of time, e. g.
α) to turn away, i. e. to pass away, Jer.
6, 4 פָּנָה הַיּוֹם the day turns, declines;
also poet. Ps. 90, 9 all our days turn
away, pass away. β) to turn in ap-
proaching, e. g. in the phrases: לִפְנוֹת
